analysis.title: GS Basics - Permitting Bill. High Beta & Momentum. Inflation Expectations Roll Over
key_insights: Markets had a strong recovery on 11/9. Tech recovered, Nvidia weakness stayed contained to the stock, and energy fell sharply. Privorotsky says GS's US prime book just saw one of the most aggressive net and gross de-risking episodes of the past decade.

October CPI is the final piece. An in-line or softer print would challenge the roughly 80% priced probability of a December Fed hike, or the risk of a March hike. Privorotsky warns vol tends to be autocorrelated after a violent rally off the lows, with hot CPI and renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend as the obvious risks.

Oil: Trump's talks with Gulf leaders suggest little appetite for escalation, and regional governments favor economic pressure on Iran over military action. Privorotsky calls it containment, not de-escalation. The market is separating shipping constraints from a true barrel shortage, so the oil risk premium has further to unwind if flows normalize. He sees risk as two-sided after a fast repricing and stays balanced.

Tech: the first neocloud to report after the midterms reports today. The question is whether contracted capacity earns attractive returns after financing costs, delays and depreciation, not whether demand exists. The market compartmentalized Nvidia's company-specific headlines (leadership uncertainty) instead of selling the whole AI complex, which Privorotsky reads as a positive signal.

Permitting: the bipartisan permitting bill cleared its first Senate procedural vote 73-25. It is not final passage and the House is likely the bigger obstacle. Privorotsky thinks the market misread the elections and expects data centers to be built with more conditions, not a nationwide moratorium. He says permitting reform benefits infrastructure and well-capitalized developers. CEG rose 10% on stronger numbers, higher guidance and additional generation agreements.

CPI: GIR forecasts October headline CPI +0.21% MoM vs +0.3% consensus and core +0.16% vs +0.22%. Drivers are shelter disinflation and softer goods prices (used cars -1.5%, medical insurance -2.5%), offset by tariffs and transportation costs. Core at 0.2% would be constructive and 0.3% would challenge the rally.

Rates: $42bn of 10-year Treasury supply today follows a relatively weak 3-year auction, and $25bn of 30-year supply comes Thursday. Brent fell almost 6% on 11/9 and the 10-year barely moved. Privorotsky concludes rates respond more to AI growth expectations than to energy.

Positioning: the drawdown was painful because momentum and high beta unwound together, which compounds across leveraged exposures and drove strong low-volatility outperformance. A re-grossing trade needs a steeper curve, recovering growth expectations and high beta and momentum regaining leadership. A CPI that lets bonds rally could turn short covering into a more durable re-grossing cycle.

Privorotsky's view: the AI narrative got confused. Undersupply is not the issue. The medium and long-term worry is compute oversupply or efficiency gains. With positioning defensive, the year-end setup looks increasingly attractive if energy and inflation align. Natural areas to chase are aerospace, transports, select discretionary and high quality unlevered AI. He is broadly encouraged but says much of the bounce has happened, making aggressive chasing hard before CPI. SPX December upside is back to 13 vol, which makes staying invested easier.
Side note: 2-year inflation pricing rolled over to summer levels. Privorotsky suggests rate hike expectations may follow.

tension_points.bull_case: GIR forecasts October CPI at +0.21% headline and +0.16% core, below consensus. Shelter disinflation, softer goods prices and falling 2-year inflation pricing could cut the roughly 80% priced December hike odds.
tension_points.bear_case: Tariffs and transportation costs offset the soft components. A hot CPI would hit a rally that came off violent lows, with vol autocorrelated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core CPI at 0.3% would challenge the rally.

tension_points.bull_case: The market is separating shipping constraints from a barrel shortage. If flows normalize without more infrastructure damage, the risk premium has further to unwind.
tension_points.bear_case: This is containment, not de-escalation, and the Houthis' behavior is unclear. Escalation into the weekend is a risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Iran targeting Gulf energy infrastructure, or renewed Middle East escalation into the weekend.

tension_points.bull_case: Positioning is defensive, energy, rates and credit are supportive, and a CPI that lets bonds rally could turn short covering into a durable re-grossing cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: Much of the initial bounce has happened, which makes aggressive chasing hard ahead of CPI.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A CPI print that fails to give bonds a reason to rally, with core at 0.3%.
